1.title: Why the D.O.J. Is Pursuing Low-Level Fraud Cases
1.summary: Our reporter Devlin Barrett explains why the Department of Justice is pursuing small-time fraud cases, and what that means for larger fraud investigations at the department.

2.title: An Unlikely Emergency Appeal to the Supreme Court from a Dog Named Bruce
2.summary: A last-ditch filing this week came on behalf of a dog that a judge found to be “vicious” and shows how the court’s emergency docket has been growing.

3.title: Brad Pitt’s Return to Drinking Is Not Unsafe, Experts Say
3.summary: His disclosure in an interview revived a key question about sobriety: whether someone who once drank dangerously can ever drink moderately.

4.title: Russia Campaigned to Derail Moldova’s Pro-Western Government
4.summary: In Moldova, Moscow paid Orthodox priests, conducted a vote-buying scheme and set up training camps on election interference — all in an effort to derail the Western-leaning government.

5.title: Stolen Matisse artworks recovered by police in Brazil
5.summary: A man is arrested after eight works by the French artist are found at a home in greater São Paulo.

6.title: More Wildfires and Extreme Heat Roil Europe, but Relief Is on the Horizon
6.summary: Another day of near record heat baked the continent on Friday, but temperatures could retreat to seasonal averages in the coming days.
